Tristram Horton Neuro

By: Tarryn Crossman | Commission

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
With 98 Neurosurgeons in South Africa, these doctors are part of an elite inner circle. They are also big money spinners for private hospitals, as neurosurgery is specialised, expensive and means ICU time.
Tristram Horton came to South Africa from the USA in 2019, marketing himself as a Neurosurgeon with a double fellowship, which is rare on the continent. After two years in state, he was quickly picked up by multiple private hospitals.

A few months ago we got a tip off that Horton was not the golden boy he was being selling himself as, and was a danger to the patients he was performing brain surgery on.

What followed was a hard investigation into an elite boys club, where no-one was willing to speak out no matter the cost to patient. The world of private medicine revealed itself to be a medical mafia, where money trumps everything. And Tristram Horton is money spinner.



Further information:
The first redflag was that Horton was not actually a highly qualified American Doctor, in fact he had lost his licence in Arizona state in 2017, after a lengthy investigation including cocaine use, cocaine rehabilitation and multiple medical malpractice cases against him. The most terrifying of which was that he Performed spinal surgery incorrectly and put the part in wrong, he then tried to cover up his mistake by taking the patient back without any scans being done.
He then went to lose his licence in Pennsylvania state in 2019, after which he moved to South Africa he approached the HOD at Barra, at the time Dr Goolab about working in South Africa. “I remember thinking this is very suspicious why does this Big shot neurosurgeon from the USA want to come and work at Bara. SO asked him straight and told him how tough it is in SA, but said he really wanted this because his mother was sick and he needed to stay in SA”

Horton somehow managed to register with the HPCSA to sit the Final neurosurgery exams at Wits medical school, under professor Ouma, which qualified him to work in South Africa. He is registered with the HPCSA and does two years of public service at Bara and Thelle Mogoerane Regional hospital.

Witness from this time period –
Professor Ouma or Poati
Medical rep 1
Talks about the medical marfia and how money trumps lives

No case studies from here, more character development
He started off charming and kind, seemed knowledgeable and a score for SA registers. But switched like jackal and Hyde. Throwing things in theatre, screaming at staff and taking exceptionally long to do procedures. Like something that on average takes no more than 4 hours, Horton was taking 14 hours to complete. With dire consequences to the patients.

STATES – while under investigation in the states he had a psych evaluation and it showed he had slow processing speeds for his speciality


Horton goes into Private, he is picked up by
Arwyp- Kempton park
Linmed - netcare
And Newcastle – Mediclinic

Rep 2 – brings us a case study who was injured after Horton made a grave surgical error.
She also brings out more truths about Horton in surgery and how everyone in the medical world knows about his failings, but won’t speak out.
The whispers in the surgical halls
And the patients being injured while everyone remains silent

Case study 1 – Ramashoba family
18 year old boy who almost died when Horton clipped the main ventricle to his brain by mistake and only realised when he went into distress an hour later

Dr Buthelezi – Neuro at Newcastle
He has reported Horton to the Hospital board but so far no further investigations have taken place
Two case studies, where Horton lied about removing the tumour and refused to allow Buthulezi to check. He basically couldn’t find the tumour and tried to cover it up. Both patients are still alive, just with symptoms of the tumor
Buthelezi also highlight Hortons failure with regards to post operative care. He drive up on the Friday, does surgeries all weekend and leaves for JHB on the Monday. Then his patients crash or get cranial bleeding and Buthulezi is left to look after them. Buthulezi called him a butcher

Case study 2 – family of the 71 year old patient may speak to us, about how Horton made them believe that their mother was absolutely fine and all the tumour was gone, when in fact he was only able to remove 50% and their mom is actually still very sick.

Last year, Mathabile Ramoshaba was due to write his matric exams. He was young, healthy and about to embrace a new chapter… until he suffered a seizure

MR
We went to a hospital. The hospital did, like some scans, and I was diagnosed with a cerebral aneurysm

1:28 – 1:40
VO2
Mathabile had a blood clot in his brain and was told he needed an immediate operation. The procedure would be done by neurosurgeon, Tristram Horton

MR
It was the cool guy. Also funny, friendly, saying, don't worry, l Everything will be fine. He had like a nice personality and was friendly.




MR MOM
the doctor assured me that it's gonna be over in a short period of time.
Within four days. He'll be back to school then.

VO3
Nothing could have been further from the truth. The surgery took a tragic toll on Mathabile’s life, and raises serious questions about Dr Horton and his methods.

Fade to black

Track of lights onto Govan walking

a few weeks back, we received a tip-off alleging that an American Neurosurgeon now practising in South Africa was endangering the lives of his patients.

DAVID
I’d be sitting in doctors' rooms where it is openly discussed how a patient is maimed or even paralysed by Horton.

2:42 – 2:53
V05
In the weeks that followed, we pieced together what we now consider one of the most disturbing investigations into alleged medical malpractice we’ve ever undertaken.

Penn state call

3:12 – 3:39
VO6
Following his fellowship at Penn State University in America, Tristram Horton completed a second specialisation in Neurosurgery at the University of Michigan. In 2013, he became a director in the neurosurgery department of the Banner Medical Group in Arizona, one of the state's top hospital groups. So, why did he suddenly appear in South Africa in 2020?




3;43 – 3;49
This is an anonymous audio recording with a neurosurgeon who met Horton soon after he arrived

I inquired about why he wanted to come from the USA.
He said no his mother is very Ill in South AFRICA and that's why he was coming here
I got a bit nervous when I see someone from the institute that he quotes me he was from - its a very prominent institute in the US.
I would find it hard to imagine that ifyou had been there you would want to com work in a state hospital in South AFrica

4;18 – 4;37
VO7
Horton started practising at Gauteng’s Thelle Mogoerwana Regional Hospital in 2021. It’s where a nurse we’ll call Anna worked with him. To protect her identity, this is the verbatim account of her experience as told by an actress.

ANNA
I first met Tristram Horton in December 2021.

He had been introduced to all the staff as a new consultant.

With his American qualifications and how he spoke, I believed he had much to teach. We were all really excited.

However after a number of cases with DR Horton

there was a downward trend,

and I realised he was dangerous

5;10 – 5;28
VO8
There are just 98 neurosurgeons in South Africa and trying to penetrate this elite community is challenging. For months, we’ve been speaking to medical professionals all gravely disturbed by Horton but still unwilling to go on record against a colleague.






ANNA
it’s like the medical mafia, and if you blow the whistle on Someone, you will never work in South Africa.
It's as simple as that. The backlash is huge

ANON DOC
You know as South africans, we’ve all heard of Colleagues when somebody has the potential to be mentally unstable …. one must be careful of those kinds of volatile personalities


5;54-6;04
VO9
It’s why we promised this doctor, who also worked at Thelle Mogorwane hospital, that we’d use a computer-generated voice to keep him safe.

Poati
He had this thing of changing personalities or moods. He was unstable

While he was at Thelle horton he was aggressive.

Yes that is right, and it was a huge problem. At some point, their was an internal investigation done, but ultimately after a year his contract was not renewed,

GOVAN
Was was Doctor Horton allowed to conduct surgeries unsupervised?
Poati
NO
Look my main goal was to protect the patients and I did that, by not letting operate alone. Thats all I could do

6;43 – 7;15
VO10
In 2022, Horton moved into independent private practice at Gauteng’s Arwyp and Linmed Netcare hospitals. He later added Mediclinic Newcastle in KZN to his portfolio

DAVID, not his real name, worked with Horton in more than one of these hospitals. Again, so concerned about speaking out, we’re using an actor to deliver the answers he gave us.

DAVID
He's a cowboy in theatre, like where most surgeons wouldn't touch something. He would brag about how this is an inoperable case; only one person has done it in the States.

7;25 – 7;32
VO11
This is one of the few recordings we have of Horton’s voice. It’s from a video of him operating on a blood clot.

VIDEO

7;42 – 8;09
VO12
David urged us to find an elderly female patient Horton had operated on. She’d been experiencing seizures from an aggressive, cancerous brain tumour and went into surgery in October last year. After the operation, Horton told her he’d successfully removed the tumour.

Her name is Marcia Cronje, and her joy at the outcome was short-lived.


MARCHIA
He told my husband and me that he had taken everything out.
GOVAN
I imagine Marsha. Hearing the news like that, you must have been relieved.
MARCHIA
I was relieved

8;26 – 8;38
VO13
But a month later, a check-up revealed that the tumour was not only still there but also bigger. This is an audio recording of a meeting Marcia had with Horton.


Recording 3
How can this thing grow so quickly
Let me just look
I didn’t even know about the scans
I did take out the entire thing
Why did they say there is regrowth
Yes
Really
Because I did take out this whole thing

8;58 – 9;06
VO14
Brain surgery is mentally and physically traumatic, and Marcia now faced going back into theatre

GOVAN
How did you feel about the prospect of going for a second operation? Myself?
MARCHIA
You don't want to know.
MARCHIA
At that stage, I was thinking of my family. I want to be there for them.


9;25-9;35
VO15
Marcia still had faith in Horton but was growing suspicious of what he was telling her. David had direct access to the theatre that day this is his recollection

DAVID
In theatre, He said look, Is everyone looking? There's no tumour.
DAVID
He said there's no tumour here, and we can just close up.

9;42 – 9;52
VO16
But this scan done by Marcia’s oncologist in April this year, the tumour in Marcia’s brain is still there and growing bigger.

MARCIA
Why? Why? He told us the thing was removed, but this ONCOLOGIST is telling me he didn't take everything out.













10;03- 10;39
VO17
Was Horton lying about removing Marcia’s tumour, or was it growing back?

While we continued investigating Marcia's case, this letter sent to Mediclinic Newcastle was leaked to us. It raised deeply disturbing claims, including this stand out allegation: Horton was lying to his patients about removing their tumours.

Beat! Ah ha moment

The letter was written by a specialist, who we’ll call Dr Andrews to protect him. He says it stemmed from concern for all Horton's patients.

For the tumours that he removed, any average neurosurgeon should be able at least to come out with a biopsy to say this is a tissue from the tumour, not to miss it entirely altogether.
GOVAN
Is that what happened?
HIDDEN ID
Yes.

11;08 -11;24
VO18
That an experienced neurosurgeon would miss tumours entirely seems unfathomable. But we were shown these brain scans of some of Horton's patients, taken by a doctor who suspected the neurosurgeon was lying.

MRI SCENE
So this is post-op
Tumours is still there and the same size

11;35- 11;37
VO19
The evidence seems undeniable.


Remember, I can talk as much as I want and even lie, but you will never bribe the images, the scans, the MRI.



11;49 – 11;55
VO20
This doctor confirmed that Horton had never removed Marcia’s aggressive cancerous tumour


It shows very well that from the first instance, it was never even touched.
any neurosurgeon would have managed to remove that tumour of MARCIA and they WOULD have removed it completely.

HIDDEN ID
This is a dire situation
GOVAN
Do you think he possesses the skills to remove these tumours?
HIDDEN ID
I think. I am a very, very, very optimistic person. I think in the future he will. But at the moment, not yet.

12;28 – 12;55
VO21
Mediclinic Newcastle confirmed they’re currently investigating the allegations made in the letter and Horton has elected not to practice there for now

But the question of why a neurosurgeon would leave a respected position in America to practise here remained. We examined his history, focussing on 2013 when it appears his troubles began at banner medical in Arizona


LINK - cocaine

13;09- 13;34 – SLIGHT DEVIATION FROM THE READ
VO22
After an extensive investigation by the Arizona Medical Board Horton was ordered to surrender his practicing license in Arizona in 2017 and then in Pennsylvania in 2019. Interestingly, a psychological evaluation conducted in that time found his reactions slow for someone performing neurosurgery.
It’s around then that he surfaced in South Africa.


DAVID
How can the Health Practitioners Council register someone who lost their licence in the USA for cocaine use and gross medical negligence.






13;46 – 14;15
VO23
The Health Practitioners Council or HPCSA is solely responsible for ensuring that only competent and legitimate practitioners are registered to practice. The first thing required from a foreign doctor is a letter of good standing. When we asked the HPCSA HOW he was registered, it asked for time to investigate

While we waited, we tried putting our evidence to Horton himself.

GOVAN - hI Dr. Horton IT IS GOVAN WHITTLE, I AM CALLING FROM CARTE BLANCHE
YES
TRISTRAM - How did you get my number
GOVAN - Sorry we can’t really tell you that
Well thats crazy im ending this conversation
GOVAN Dr Horton hold on

14;44-15;06
VO24
19-year-old Mathabile Ramashoba is another of Horton’s patients. In October last year, he was operated on to fix a blood clot on his brain. It involved putting a clip in place but, after the surgery, Horton told Mathabile’s family the clip had slipped, and he’d need to go back into theatre

BOY
. He then told my mom, like, if you don't open your son into the surgery, he could die in the next coming days.

15;16 – 15;22
VO25
David was in theatre that day. His recollection of the incident is very different to Horton’s.

David
A few hours after the first surgery I was told Horton is taking the patient back in, because the way he clipped he didn’t clip the Aneurysm he clipped the main blood vessel.


15;34 – 15;47
VO26
Astonishingly, Horton had allegedly placed the clip in the wrong place and halted blood supply to a section of Mathabile’s brain. He woke up paralysed.


Mathabeli’s – strap check spelling
I turned my head and tried to move like nothing was moving. And I started crying.

15;54- 15;59
VO27
Mathabile had no idea what happened to him or why he couldn’t move

Mathabeli’s
When I turned, I saw the doctor. He was talking to himself, worried. You can see, on his face, that the person is worried, wondering what went wrong and all this stuff.
GOVAN
Who is he talking to?
boy
He. He was talking to himself.
Like what happens? Everything was going accordingly. What went wrong? All this stuff.

GOVAN
He was asking himself.
BOY
Yes.
MOM
he's disabled, he can't walk, he can't talk, he can't do anything for himself.

16;24-16;33
VO28
Within a few days of the second surgery, Mathabile was transferred to a step-down facility where he had to learn to walk again. And Horton came to visit him

BOY
He came. I was like, what did you do to me? Was like, I don't know what you been like. He didn't, like, talk a lot. I was like, I don't know, much better, but you'll be fine, see?

00:29:15:21 - 00:29:33:04
BOY
Right. You'll be fine. I was in, told him, like, get out, get out.

17;00 – 17;50
VO29
Mathabile never wrote his matric exams and is still battling to function as he did before the surgery

Arwyp Hospital confirmed that Horton is an independent practitioner at their hospital, and they can’t comment on his behalf. On Mathabile’s case, they declined to comment as there are legal proceedings underway

Linmed Netcare says it has had no issues with Horton, and he’s currently an independent practitioner with the hospital

HPCSA turned down an interview but acknowledged an error with Horton’s registration and thanked us for alerting them.

But, it’s an error that has had life-changing consequences for some of his patients. We felt compelled to get a more detailed response, so we called HPCSA spokesperson Priscilla Sekhonyana.

Phone call WITH PRISCILLIA

18;24- 19;26 – last bit about marcia is missing form the guide but the time is right as above
VO30
Eventually, the HPCSA confirmed that, as yet no action had been taken against Horton, but an investigation is underway

Horton denied all these allegations through his lawyer, stating that he is being persecuted to damage his career. He says his registration with HPCSA was recently upheld, it had independently vetted his credentials and that the HPCSA had closed a complaint by one of the patients in our stoy without any penalty.
Dr Horton claims that his licence in Arizona was reinstated that there was no internal grievance or disciplinary action against him for any behavioural issues, and that all sessional consultant contracts at Thelle Mogoerane were not renewed, not only his.
He declined to comment on any of his patients, as he is bound by his professional oath.



Add the time here for more of a gap

Marcia has been told by another neurosurgeon that she’ll need a 3rd operation.

Marcia
I don’t think I can go through it again
I don’t trust any doctors

19;41 – 19;54
VO31
And a medical expert we spoke to says the blood clot in Mathabile’s brain is still intact and life-threatening. Sadly, he’s refusing to go back to hospital

- I don’t know, but he ruined my life

VO36


The theatre and lights go off - just theatre audio

metadata.Summary: With 98 Neurosurgeons in South Africa, these doctors are part of an elite inner circle. They are also big money spinners for private hospitals, as neurosurgery is specialised, expensive and means ICU time. Tristram Horton came to South Africa from the USA in 2019, marketing himself as a Neurosurgeon with a double fellowship, which is rare on the continent. After two years in state, he was quickly picked up by multiple private hospitals. A few months ago we got a tip off that Horton was not the golden boy he was being selling himself as, and was a danger to the patients he was performing brain surgery on. What followed was a hard investigation into an elite boys club, where no-one was willing to speak out no matter the cost to patient. The world of private medicine revealed itself to be a medical mafia, where money trumps everything. And Tristram Horton is money spinner.
metadata.Further information: The first redflag was that Horton was not actually a highly qualified American Doctor, in fact he had lost his licence in Arizona state in 2017, after a lengthy investigation including cocaine use, cocaine rehabilitation and multiple medical malpractice cases against him. The most terrifying of which was that he Performed spinal surgery incorrectly and put the part in wrong, he then tried to cover up his mistake by taking the patient back without any scans being done. He then went to lose his licence in Pennsylvania state in 2019, after which he moved to South Africa he approached the HOD at Barra, at the time Dr Goolab about working in South Africa. “I remember thinking this is very suspicious why does this Big shot neurosurgeon from the USA want to come and work at Bara. SO asked him straight and told him how tough it is in SA, but said he really wanted this because his mother was sick and he needed to stay in SA” Horton somehow managed to register with the HPCSA to sit the Final neurosurgery exams at Wits medical school, under professor Ouma, which qualified him to work in South Africa. He is registered with the HPCSA and does two years of public service at Bara and Thelle Mogoerane Regional hospital. Witness from this time period – Professor Ouma or Poati Medical rep 1 Talks about the medical marfia and how money trumps lives No case studies from here, more character development He started off charming and kind, seemed knowledgeable and a score for SA registers. But switched like jackal and Hyde. Throwing things in theatre, screaming at staff and taking exceptionally long to do procedures. Like something that on average takes no more than 4 hours, Horton was taking 14 hours to complete. With dire consequences to the patients. STATES – while under investigation in the states he had a psych evaluation and it showed he had slow processing speeds for his speciality Horton goes into Private, he is picked up by Arwyp- Kempton park Linmed - netcare And Newcastle – Mediclinic Rep 2 – brings us a case study who was injured after Horton made a grave surgical error. She also brings out more truths about Horton in surgery and how everyone in the medical world knows about his failings, but won’t speak out. The whispers in the surgical halls And the patients being injured while everyone remains silent Case study 1 – Ramashoba family 18 year old boy who almost died when Horton clipped the main ventricle to his brain by mistake and only realised when he went into distress an hour later Dr Buthelezi – Neuro at Newcastle He has reported Horton to the Hospital board but so far no further investigations have taken place Two case studies, where Horton lied about removing the tumour and refused to allow Buthulezi to check. He basically couldn’t find the tumour and tried to cover it up. Both patients are still alive, just with symptoms of the tumor Buthelezi also highlight Hortons failure with regards to post operative care. He drive up on the Friday, does surgeries all weekend and leaves for JHB on the Monday. Then his patients crash or get cranial bleeding and Buthulezi is left to look after them. Buthulezi called him a butcher Case study 2 – family of the 71 year old patient may speak to us, about how Horton made them believe that their mother was absolutely fine and all the tumour was gone, when in fact he was only able to remove 50% and their mom is actually still very sick.
